newsitem.title: USA: Support for Ohio casinos grows in latest poll.
newsitem.headline: Support for Ohio casinos grows in latest poll.

text.p: While most Ohio voters still oppose a proposed constitutional amendment allowing casino gambling in the state, proponents of the measure gained some ground, according to results from a poll released Thursday.
The poll, conducted by Institute for Policy Research at University of Cincinnati, found that support for the amendment has grown to 45 percent from 38 percent of likely voters.
Still, 51 percent of voters said they oppose the measure on the Nov 5 ballot, while four percent were undecided, according to the poll which surveyed 606 likely voters between Oct 25 and 29.
The potential sampling error for the survey, sponsored by the Cincinnati Enquirer, WLWT-TV and the University of Cincinnati, was four percent.
The proposed amendment would allow a total of eight permanently moored floating casinos in Ohio that would turn over 20 percent of their gross revenues to a new Ohio Gaming Commission.
Of those revenues, 80 percent would be earmarked for public schools, with the rest split between local governments where the casinos would be located.
